instrument.name: IFSCA (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021
instrument.version: Consolidated as amended up to 7 May 2026

build_meta.statutory_text_verification: Numeric/threshold fidelity check vs source PDF: 0 unmatched figures across all provisions.
build_meta.amendment_currency: Consolidated to 7 May 2026; SPV/TCSP framework and SPV leasing tier inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026; activities and Schedule substituted w.e.f. 4 July 2022.

regulation_content.regulation_text:
1. Short title and commencement
(1). These regulations may be called the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021.
(2). They shall come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Gives the Regulations their short title and provides that they come into force on publication in the Official Gazette.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Notified 25 March 2021; in force on Gazette publication (31 March 2021)

regulation_content.simple_explanation: Defines the terms used across the Regulations. The load-bearing definitions are Finance Company (a separately incorporated financial institution) and Finance Unit (a branch), both barred from accepting public deposits and from being a Banking Unit; Owned fund; Public deposit; Aircraft Lease and Ship Lease (each covering operating, financial and hybrid leases); and the newly inserted SPV and TCSP definitions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The Finance Company / Finance Unit split runs through the entire framework — a Finance Company is a separately incorporated entity, a Finance Unit is a branch of a home-jurisdiction entity, and almost every downstream obligation reads differently for the two. The SPV and TCSP definitions were inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026 and open up the SPV leasing/financing route that the aircraft- and ship-leasing market has been waiting for. Note too that the public-deposit bar is built into the definitions themselves — it is a structural feature, not a separate prohibition.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Finance Company = separately incorporated; Finance Unit = branch; neither may take public deposits; SPV & TCSP inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units
regulation_content.effective_date: SPV and TCSP definitions inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026 (Notification IFSCA/GN/2026/009)

regulation_content.chapter_title: Setting Up Of A Finance Company
regulation_content.regulation_text:
3. Registration Requirement
(1) An entity shall commence business as a Finance Company or Finance Unit, as the case may be, in International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) only after obtaining a certificate of registration from the Authority for carrying out the activities specified in Schedule to these regulations.
Provided that a certificate of registration under these regulations shall be required to be obtained by an entity intending to carry out such permissible activities which are not covered under the framework or regulations under which it was previously granted registration or authorisation, if any.
Explanation: An entity that has obtained a certificate of registration or authorisation for a specific activity under another framework or regulations, issued or notified by the Authority, shall not be required to seek a fresh registration under these regulations for carrying out the same activity, if it is a permissible activity under regulation 5 of these regulations.
(2) A Finance Company can be set up either as a subsidiary or a joint venture, or as a newly incorporated company under the Companies Act, 2013, or in any other form as may be specified by the Authority from time to time,
Provided that if the parent of a Finance Company is carrying out a regulated financial activity in its home jurisdiction, it shall obtain a No-objection Certificate from its home country regulator for setting up a Finance Company in the IFSCs, wherever applicable.
(3) A Finance Unit can be set up if the applicant is an incorporated entity in its home jurisdiction.
Provided that a Finance Unit can be set up for undertaking core activities as specified in these regulations only if the applicant, being an incorporated entity in its home jurisdiction, is engaged in the business of financial services and is regulated by a financial sector regulator in its home jurisdiction and has obtained a No-Objection Certificate from the home regulator for setting up a Finance Unit in the IFSCs, wherever applicable.
Provided further that the conditions under the above proviso shall not apply to an incorporated entity which desires to set up a Global/Regional Corporate Treasury Centre as a Finance Unit in the IFSCs for undertaking treasury activities or treasury services in accordance with the relevant regulatory framework specified by the Authority.
(4) An application for grant of registration as a Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, shall be made by the applicant in the form and manner as specified by the Authority.
Provided that an applicant intending to undertake either one or more non-core activities may be considered for registration as ‘finance company’ for the purposes of these regulations even if incorporated in the form of a Limited Liability Partnership or a Trust.
(5) A Finance Company or a Finance Unit seeking registration shall comply with following conditions:
(i) The applicant seeking registration as a ‘Finance Company’ shall have and maintain minimum owned fund, depending on the category of activity(ies) or a combination of activities classified under different categories under these regulations, and shall maintain the higher of the minimum capital or owned funds or net worth prescribed for each activity or category of activities specified in Schedule under these regulations or under any of the relevant regulatory framework issued by the Authority, as applicable.
(ii) In case the applicant, being an incorporated entity in its home jurisdiction, is seeking to set up and register a ‘Finance Unit’, it shall provide and maintain minimum owned fund on unimpaired basis at all times, depending on the category of activity(ies) or a combination of activities classified under different categories under these regulations, and shall maintain the higher of the minimum capital or owned funds or net worth prescribed for each activity or category of activities specified in Schedule under these regulations or under any of the relevant regulatory framework issued by the Authority, as applicable.
(6) The applicant entity and/or its promoters shall be from a FATF compliant jurisdiction and comply with international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force to combat money laundering and terrorist financing.
(7) After considering the application made under sub-regulation (4), if the Authority is satisfied that the terms and conditions as specified in these regulations have been complied with, it may grant certificate of registration to the applicant, in such form and subject to such conditions, as may be specified:
Provided that on a request received from an applicant, if the Authority is satisfied that the applicant may be given more time to comply with certain conditions for grant of registration, it may, for the reasons to be recorded in writing, consider grant of provisional registration giving additional time to the applicant, subject to such conditions, as it may deem necessary:
Provided further that the provisional registration can be withdrawn by the Authority if the Authority is satisfied that the applicant is unable to comply with any of the conditions under which the provisional registration was granted.
(8) After considering the application for registration, if the Authority is of the opinion that registration cannot be granted, it shall communicate the deficiencies to the applicant giving it thirty days’ time to rectify them.
(9) If the applicant fails to rectify such deficiencies to the satisfaction of the Authority within the specified time, the Authority may refuse to grant certificate of registration and shall communicate the same to the applicant, giving reasons for such refusal:
Provided that no such refusal shall be made by the Authority without giving the applicant an opportunity to make written submissions on the grounds on which the registration is proposed to be refused.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the registration requirement and eligibility. No entity may commence business as a Finance Company or Finance Unit without a certificate of registration for the activities in the Schedule. A Finance Company is set up as a subsidiary, joint venture, newly incorporated company or other permitted form; a Finance Unit is a branch of an entity incorporated (and, for core activities, financial-sector regulated) in its home jurisdiction. Where the parent carries on a regulated financial activity, a home-regulator NOC is required. An applicant doing only non-core activities may be registered even as an LLP or Trust. Minimum owned fund must be maintained per the Schedule, on an unimpaired basis at all times for a Finance Unit. The Authority may grant provisional registration; deficiencies carry a thirty-day cure period.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: Two structuring points do the heavy lifting. First, the LLP/Trust concession is available only for non-core-only applicants — the moment a core activity is added, the company form (and the higher capital) is back. Second, a registration is activity-scoped: the proviso and Explanation inserted in 2022 mean an entity already authorised for an activity under another IFSCA framework need not re-register for that same activity, but does need registration for any new permissible activity outside its existing authorisation. The GRCTC carve-out from the home-regulator/financial-sector conditions is easy to miss.
regulation_content.practical_point: Fix the Finance Company vs Finance Unit choice and the core/non-core activity mix first, because together they drive legal form, the owned-fund tier and the NOC requirement. For a non-core-only play, an LLP or Trust is available; the moment a core activity is contemplated, plan for a company and the USD 3 million tier. Check whether an existing IFSCA authorisation already covers the activity before filing afresh.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Obtain the certificate of registration before commencing business; maintain the Schedule owned-fund minimum at all times (unimpaired, for a Finance Unit); obtain the home-regulator NOC where the parent is regulated; respond to any deficiency letter within thirty days.
regulation_content.example: A promoter wanting only aircraft operating-lease (non-core) business can register as an LLP with USD 0.2 million owned fund. Adding a core lending activity forces a company structure and the USD 3 million tier.
regulation_content.risk_point: The common failures are choosing an LLP/Trust and then adding a core activity without re-capitalising and re-forming, and filing a fresh application for an activity already covered by an existing IFSCA authorisation. For a Finance Unit, letting owned fund dip below the minimum intra-year breaches the 'unimpaired at all times' condition.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical interview question: a client wants to do only aircraft operating lease from GIFT IFSC — what structure and minimum owned fund would you advise, and how does the answer change if it also wants to lend?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Registration mandatory; Finance Unit owned fund unimpaired at all times; non-core-only may be LLP/Trust; home-regulator NOC where parent regulated; 30 days to cure deficiencies; provisional registration possible
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Company / Finance Unit applicants
regulation_content.effective_date: Registration proviso/Explanation inserted w.e.f. 4 July 2022; set-up conditions substituted w.e.f. 4 July 2022

regulation_content.regulation_text:
4. Applicable prudential regulations
(1) The prudential regulations applicable to a Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, shall be such as may be specified by the Authority.
(2) Capital Ratio (CR)
A Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, shall maintain a minimum capital ratio at eight per cent. of its regulatory capital to its risk-weighted assets or at such per centage as may be specified by the Authority.
(3) Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)
A Finance Company or a Finance Unit as the case may be, shall maintain LCR on stand-alone basis, at all times, as may be determined by the Authority.
Provided that in the case of a Finance Unit, the LCR may be allowed to be maintained by the parent entity, with specific approval of the Authority.
(4) Exposure Ceiling (EC)
The sum of all the exposures of a Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, to a single counterparty or group of connected counterparties shall not exceed twenty-five per cent. of its available eligible capital base without the approval of the Authority.
Explanation: The Authority shall issue operational guidelines with respect to the implementation of the requirements under sub-regulations (1) to (4) of regulation 4.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the prudential requirements. The Authority specifies the applicable prudential regulations; a Finance Company or Finance Unit must maintain a minimum capital ratio of eight per cent of regulatory capital to risk-weighted assets (or as specified); maintain the Liquidity Coverage Ratio on a stand-alone basis at all times (a Finance Unit may, with specific approval, maintain LCR at parent level); and keep total exposure to a single or connected group of counterparties within twenty-five per cent of its eligible capital base without the Authority's approval.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: These are the three prudential dials — an 8% capital floor, a stand-alone LCR, and a 25% single/connected-party exposure ceiling. The stand-alone LCR is the one Finance Units try to push up to the parent; that needs specific approval and should not be assumed. The operational detail sits in guidelines the Authority issues under the Explanation, so the base figures here are the floor, not the full picture.
regulation_content.practical_point: Build capital-ratio, LCR and large-exposure monitoring into the monthly MIS from day one. For a Finance Unit intending parent-level LCR, secure the specific approval rather than assuming it. Track the 25% exposure line against connected-counterparty groupings, not just single names.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain capital ratio >= 8% and LCR at all times; keep single/connected-counterparty exposure <= 25% of eligible capital base absent Authority approval; follow the operational guidelines issued under this regulation.
regulation_content.example: A Finance Company with an eligible capital base of USD 40 million cannot take more than USD 10 million of exposure to one connected counterparty group without the Authority's approval.
regulation_content.risk_point: Breaching the 25% exposure ceiling or letting the capital ratio slip below 8% are the sharp prudential exposures an inspection quantifies directly. For a Finance Unit, relying on parent-level LCR without specific approval is a compliance gap.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to state the three prudential numbers — 8% capital ratio, stand-alone LCR, 25% exposure ceiling — and explain the Finance Unit LCR concession and its precondition.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Capital ratio >= 8% of RWA; LCR stand-alone at all times (Finance Unit parent-level with approval); single/connected exposure <= 25% of eligible capital base
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets out the permissible activities — core and non-core. Core activities include lending (loans, commitments, guarantees, credit enhancement, securitisation, financial lease and sale/purchase of portfolios), factoring and forfaiting, investments, buying/selling derivatives, and Global/Regional Corporate Treasury Centres. Non-core activities include merchant banking, RTA, trusteeship, investment advisory, portfolio management, operating lease of any products (including aircraft and ship lease), international trade financing, distribution of financial products, trading/clearing membership, ancillary asset-management support, and — inserted in 2026 — leasing or financing activity undertaken by an SPV. Non-core activities require a separately identifiable department, firewalls against conflicts, and a Board-approved grievance/compensation policy; each non-core activity is also subject to its own framework. Dealings with residents attract FEMA; only hedging derivatives are allowed for non-core entities; speculative transactions are barred.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The core/non-core classification is the practical fault line — it drives the owned-fund tier in the Schedule, the exempted regulations, and whether the LLP/Trust form is available. Operating lease (including aircraft and ship) sits on the non-core side, which is why a pure lessor can use the lighter USD 0.2 million tier, while financial lease is a core activity carrying the USD 3 million tier. The 2026 amendment added the SPV leasing/financing route as a non-core activity, aligning the regime with orphan-SPV structures common in aviation and shipping finance.
regulation_content.practical_point: Classify every intended activity as core or non-core before anything else, since that classification cascades into capital, structure and exempted regulations. For non-core activities, set up the SID, firewalls and Board-approved grievance policy, and check the activity-specific framework. Distinguish operating lease (non-core) from financial lease (core) deliberately — the capital consequence is material.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Run each non-core activity through a separately identifiable department with firewalls and a Board-approved grievance/compensation policy; comply with the activity-specific framework; restrict derivatives to hedging for non-core entities; undertake no speculative or speculative-funding transactions; apply FEMA to resident dealings.
regulation_content.example: An SPV set up through a TCSP to own and lease a single aircraft can register for the SPV leasing/financing non-core activity with owned fund set at the Companies Act, 2013 paid-up capital level, rather than the USD 3 million core tier.
regulation_content.risk_point: Misclassifying financial lease as operating lease understates the required owned fund by an order of magnitude and is a serious registration defect. Running multiple non-core activities without genuine SID separation and firewalls invites conflict-of-interest findings. Any speculative position is a direct breach.
regulation_content.interview_point: The interviewer may test whether you can separate core from non-core activities for a leasing business, and explain why operating lease and financial lease attract different owned-fund tiers.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Core: lending/financial lease/factoring/investments/derivatives/GRCTC. Non-core: operating lease (incl. aircraft/ship), advisory, PMS, distribution, SPV leasing (2026), etc. Non-core needs SID + firewall + Board grievance policy; hedging-only derivatives; no speculation
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units
regulation_content.effective_date: SPV leasing/financing non-core activity inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026; activity list substituted w.e.f. 4 July 2022

regulation_content.regulation_text:
6. Currency of Operations
(1) A Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, shall carry out its operation in a freely convertible foreign currency and with such persons, whether resident or otherwise, as may be permitted by the Authority:
Provided that a Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, may be permitted to conduct such business transactions denominated in INR as may be specified by the Authority, subject to settlement of those business transactions in freely convertible foreign currency.
(2) A Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, shall be permitted to have an INR account out of the freely convertible foreign currency to defray their administrative and statutory expenses and for such other purposes as may be specified by the Authority.
(3) Every Finance Company or a Finance Unit shall maintain its balance sheet only in United States Dollars (USD). A Finance Unit shall ensure that accounts pertaining to its transactions are kept distinct from that of its parent.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the currency regime. A Finance Company or Finance Unit operates in a freely convertible foreign currency (INR business only as specifically permitted, settled in foreign currency); may hold an INR account out of foreign currency for administrative and statutory expenses; and must maintain its balance sheet only in USD. A Finance Unit must keep its transaction accounts distinct from the parent's.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The USD balance-sheet mandate and the account-separation rule for a Finance Unit are the practical anchors — a Finance Unit that commingles its books with the parent's breaches this even if every transaction is otherwise compliant.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain the balance sheet in USD; keep a Finance Unit's transaction accounts distinct from the parent's; restrict INR dealings to the permitted, foreign-currency-settled cases.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Balance sheet only in USD; freely convertible FCY operations; INR account for expenses; Finance Unit accounts kept distinct from parent
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.provision_heading: Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering
regulation_content.regulation_text:
7. Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering
Every Finance Company and Finance Unit shall follow Know Your Customer norms, combating of financing of terrorism and other anti-money laundering requirements, including reporting requirements, as specified for a Banking Unit in IFSCs.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires every Finance Company and Finance Unit to follow the KYC, CFT and other AML requirements, including reporting, as specified for a Banking Unit in IFSCs.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The standard borrows the Banking Unit AML regime wholesale, so the benchmark is bank-grade, not a lighter NBFC-style approach. Build the AML programme to the Banking Unit specification.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Implement KYC/CFT/AML controls and reporting to the Banking Unit standard specified for IFSCs.
regulation_content.important_numbers: AML/KYC/CFT to the Banking Unit standard
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.regulation_text:
8. Corporate Governance and Disclosure Requirements
(1) Every Finance Company and Finance Unit shall adhere to the guidelines on corporate governance and disclosure requirements to be specified by the Authority.
(2) Any mergers, acquisitions, takeovers or change in management of a Finance Company, which results in its change in control of at least twenty per-cent. of total share capital, or of business decisions under an agreement, shall be subject to prior approval and such other requirements as may be specified by the Authority:
Provided that mergers, acquisitions, takeovers or change in management in the parent of a Finance Unit shall be in compliance to its registration requirements and shall be intimated to the Authority within a period of 15 days from the date of such event.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires adherence to the Authority's corporate governance and disclosure guidelines. Any merger, acquisition, takeover or change in management of a Finance Company that results in a change in control of at least twenty per cent of total share capital, or of business decisions under an agreement, needs prior approval. For a Finance Unit, such changes in the parent must comply with registration requirements and be intimated to the Authority within fifteen days of the event.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The twenty per cent change-in-control trigger is the one company-secretarial teams most often need to catch, and it captures control of business decisions under agreement, not just share transfers. The Finance Company route is prior approval; the Finance Unit route for parent-level change is a fifteen-day post-event intimation — a genuinely different mechanic that turns on the entity type.
regulation_content.practical_point: Map the control chain and shareholders'/management agreements so a 20% change-in-control event is identified before completion. Route Finance Company control changes as prior-approval applications; diarise the fifteen-day intimation for Finance Unit parent-level changes.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Obtain prior approval for a >=20% change in control (including control of business decisions) of a Finance Company; for a Finance Unit, intimate parent-level M&A/management changes to the Authority within fifteen days.
regulation_content.example: A 22% share acquisition in a Finance Company needs prior approval; a change of control at the parent of a Finance Unit needs a fifteen-day intimation instead.
regulation_content.risk_point: Completing a 20%-plus control change without prior approval, or missing the fifteen-day parent-change intimation for a Finance Unit, are the recurring governance breaches — and both are easy for an inspection to date-check.
regulation_content.interview_point: A practical question: at what shareholding change does a Finance Company need prior approval, and how is a Finance Unit treated differently when the change is at the parent?
regulation_content.important_numbers: Change in control >= 20% of total share capital: prior approval (Finance Company); Finance Unit parent change: intimate within 15 days
regulation_content.applicability: Finance Companies (prior approval); Finance Units (15-day intimation for parent change)

regulation_content.regulation_text:
9. Reporting Requirements
(1) Every Finance Company and Finance Unit shall furnish information relating to its operations to the Authority, in such manner, interval and form, as may be specified by the Authority.
(2) Every financial reporting by a Finance Company and a Finance Unit to the Authority shall be in US Dollar, unless otherwise specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Requires every Finance Company and Finance Unit to furnish operational information to the Authority in the specified manner, interval and form, with all financial reporting in US Dollars unless otherwise specified.
regulation_content.compliance_point: File the specified periodic returns in the required form; report financials in USD.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Reporting in USD unless otherwise specified
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to Specify Procedures and Issue Clarifications
regulation_content.regulation_text:
10. Power to Specify Procedures and Issue Clarifications
(1) For the purposes of implementation of these regulations and matters incidental thereto, or in order to facilitate and regulate financial services relating to activities permitted under these regulations, the Authority may specify norms, procedures, processes, manners including relaxations therefrom, if any, by way of circulars or guidelines.
(2) The applicant entity /Finance Company/ Finance Unit, shall pay to the Authority, such fees and charges, as may be specified.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Empowers the Authority to specify norms, procedures, processes and manners (including relaxations) by circular or guideline for implementing the Regulations, and requires payment of specified fees and charges.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: As with the other IFSC frameworks, much of the operative detail lives in circulars issued under this power, so compliance monitoring must track IFSCA circulars alongside the base text.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may issue circulars/guidelines and relaxations; fees payable as specified
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.provision_heading: Power to remove difficulties and relax strict enforcement of the regulations
regulation_content.regulation_text:
10A. Power to remove difficulties and relax strict enforcement of the regulations
(1) In order to remove any difficulty in the application or interpretations of the provisions of these regulations, the Authority may issue clarifications through guidance notes or circulars.
(2) The Authority, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may in the interest of development of financial market, relax the strict enforcement of any requirement of these regulations, upon payment of fee, if any, as may be specified by the Authority.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Lets the Authority issue clarifications through guidance notes or circulars to remove difficulties in applying or interpreting the Regulations, and — for reasons recorded in writing and in the interest of financial-market development — relax the strict enforcement of any requirement, on payment of any specified fee.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: A relaxation is available but is reasoned, discretionary and development-oriented — it is not a general waiver to be assumed in structuring. Approach it with a specific, well-argued case.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Authority may relax strict enforcement for recorded reasons
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.regulation_text:
11. Action in Case of Default
If a Finance Company or a Finance Unit, as the case may be, fails to fulfil any of the conditions subject to which the registration under Regulation 3 has been granted, the Authority may take any action as it may deem fit, including suspension, withdrawal or cancellation of registration, after giving an opportunity to the entity, of making its submissions.
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Where a Finance Company or Finance Unit fails to fulfil any condition of its Regulation 3 registration, the Authority may take any action it deems fit — including suspension, withdrawal or cancellation of registration — after giving the entity an opportunity to make submissions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: The trigger is any breach of a registration condition, so the continuing conditions in Regulations 4 to 9 all feed into this — a sustained prudential or reporting lapse is a registration-condition failure, not a stand-alone issue.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Treat every continuing condition (capital, LCR, exposure, currency, AML, governance, reporting) as a registration condition; use the opportunity to make submissions before any adverse order.
regulation_content.risk_point: Because suspension, withdrawal or cancellation all flow from a registration-condition breach, persistent prudential or reporting non-compliance can escalate to loss of registration.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Suspension / withdrawal / cancellation for registration-condition breach, after opportunity to be heard
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units

regulation_content.provision_heading: Schedule — Minimum Owned Fund Requirement by Activity
regulation_content.regulation_text:
SCHEDULE
[See regulation 3(1), 3(5)(i) and 3(5)(ii)]

No. 1 — Undertaking one or more of the non-core activities only – without any core activity(ies):
(1) Higher of USD 0.2 million or any such amount as may be required to seek specific registration for a proposed noncore activity under the respective Framework/Regulation for that particular activity; or
(2) Any higher amount as may be specified by the Authority.
Exempted regulations: Regulation (4) and Regulation (8), subject to the following:
(i) To have a Board approved prudential policy
(ii) Fit and Proper criteria set out by the Authority.

No. 2 — Undertaking one or more core activities with or without noncore activities, except for Global/Regional Corporate Treasury Centres:
(1) Higher of USD 3 million, minimum regulatory capital for core activities as specified by the Authority; or any such amount as may be required for a non-core activity(ies) under the respective Framework/Regulation for that particular activity; or
(2) Any higher amount as may be specified by the Authority.
Exempted regulations: None.

No. 3 — Undertaking activities of Global/Regional Corporate Treasury Centres:
Higher of USD 0.2 million or any such amount as may be required under the relevant regulatory framework specified by the Authority.
Exempted regulations: Regulation (4), subject to the following:
(i) To have a Board approved prudential policy
(ii) Fit and Proper criteria set out by the Authority.

No. 4 — leasing or financing activity undertaken by an SPV:
The minimum owned fund, or paid-up share capital, shall be equivalent to the amount prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, or such other amount as may be specified by the Authority.
Exempted regulations: Regulation (4) and Regulation (8).
regulation_content.simple_explanation: Sets the minimum owned-fund requirement by activity tier: non-core-only, higher of USD 0.2 million (or the amount required for the specific non-core framework); one or more core activities (except GRCTC), higher of USD 3 million (or the specified regulatory capital / non-core amount); GRCTC, higher of USD 0.2 million (or the relevant framework amount); and — inserted in 2026 — leasing or financing by an SPV, owned fund/paid-up capital equivalent to the Companies Act, 2013 amount. The non-core-only, GRCTC and SPV tiers carry exemptions from Regulation 4 and/or Regulation 8 with Board-approved prudential policy and fit-and-proper conditions.
regulation_content.regmate_comment: This is where the core/non-core classification is priced. The step from USD 0.2 million (non-core-only) to USD 3 million (any core activity) is the single most consequential number in the framework for a leasing structure. The 2026 SPV tier deliberately sets capital at the Companies Act level, which makes single-asset aircraft and ship SPVs viable without the USD 3 million core floor, and exempts them from the prudential (Reg 4) and governance (Reg 8) requirements.
regulation_content.practical_point: Price the structure off the correct tier at the outset: USD 0.2 million if it stays non-core-only, USD 3 million once any core activity is added, and the Companies Act amount for an SPV leasing/financing vehicle. Note the exempted-regulation conditions (Board-approved prudential policy, fit-and-proper) that attach to the lighter tiers.
regulation_content.compliance_point: Maintain the owned fund at the tier matching the actual activity mix; where relying on a tier that exempts Regulation 4/8, satisfy the Board-approved prudential policy and fit-and-proper conditions.
regulation_content.example: A single-aircraft leasing SPV incorporated through a TCSP capitalises to the Companies Act paid-up level and is exempt from Regulations 4 and 8; a company doing core lending must hold USD 3 million.
regulation_content.risk_point: Registering at the USD 0.2 million non-core tier and then undertaking a core activity is an owned-fund shortfall of at least USD 2.8 million — a fundamental registration defect, not a rounding issue.
regulation_content.interview_point: You should be able to map an activity mix to the correct owned-fund tier and explain why the SPV tier added in 2026 matters for aircraft and ship leasing.
regulation_content.important_numbers: Non-core only: >= USD 0.2m; any core activity: >= USD 3m; GRCTC: >= USD 0.2m; SPV leasing/financing: Companies Act paid-up amount
regulation_content.applicability: All Finance Companies and Finance Units
regulation_content.effective_date: SPV tier (item 4) inserted w.e.f. 7 May 2026; Schedule substituted w.e.f. 4 July 2022

definitions_reference.definition_text: (a) “Act” means the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 (50 of 2019);
(b) “Aircraft Lease” includes operating and financial lease and any hybrid of operating and financial lease of aircraft or helicopter and engines of aircraft or helicopter or any other part thereof;
(c) “Authority” means the International Financial Services Centres Authority established under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Act;

(d) “Banking Unit” shall have the same meaning as assigned to it under clause (c) of sub-regulation (1) of regulation 2 of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Banking) Regulations, 2020;

(e) “Finance Company” means a financial institution as defined under clause (c) of subsection (1) of section 3 of the Act, separately incorporated to deal in one or more of the permissible activities specified under sub-regulation (1) of regulation 5 of these regulations, provided: (i) It does not accept public deposit from resident and non-resident, as defined in these regulations; and (ii) It is not registered with the Authority as a Banking Unit;

(f) “Finance Unit” means a financial institution as defined under clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Act, set up as a branch permitted under these regulations to deal in one or more of the permissible activities specified under sub-regulation (1) of regulation 5 of these regulations, provided: (i) it does not accept public deposit from resident and non-resident as defined in these regulations; and (ii) it is not registered with the Authority as a Banking Unit;
(g) “International Financial Services Centre” shall have the same meaning as assigned to it under clause (g) of sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Act;
(h) “Non-resident” means a person resident outside India as defined under clause (w) of Section 2 of The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999;

(i) “Owned fund” for a Finance Company shall mean the paid-up-capital and free reserves balance in share premium account and capital reserves representing surplus arising out of sale proceeds of asset, excluding reserves created by revaluation of asset, as reduced by accumulated loss balance, book value of intangible assets and deferred revenue expenditure, if any;

(j) “Public deposit”, for the purposes of these regulations shall mean an amount raised from a resident or a non-resident, in any form which is repayable on demand or is a term deposit and includes such other amount as may be specified by the Authority from time to time;
(k) “Resident” means a person resident in India as defined under clause (v) of Section 2 of The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999;
(l) “Reserve Bank” means the Reserve Bank of India established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934);
(m) “Ship Lease” includes operating and financial lease and any hybrid of operating and financial lease of ships or ocean vessels and engines of ships or ocean vessels or any other part thereof;

(nn) “Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)” means a Finance Company incorporated or administered or both, by a Trust and Company Service Provider, in such manner as may be specified by the Authority, for undertaking permissible activities;

(o) “Trust and Company Service Provider (TCSP)” means an entity authorised under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (TechFin and Ancillary Services) Regulations, 2025, to provide TCSP services;
